content.user_title: Improve React Correctness and Rendering Performance
content.value_statement: React components can lose state, mishandle effects, or respond slowly when rendering costs are misunderstood. This skill guides version-aware reviews and targeted fixes with behavioral checks and comparable performance measurements.
actual_capabilities: Guide reviews of state ownership, derived values, stable keys, component identity, and effect dependencies.
Recommend cleanup for subscriptions, timers, and pending work, plus race handling for fetch effects.
Assess data-loading waterfalls, concurrent requests, and lazy loading against the existing framework and data layer.
Check version requirements for React 19 APIs, React Compiler, and view transitions.
Use profiler evidence to distinguish rendering costs from event computation, layout, paint, and network delay.
Recommend targeted rendering changes and before-and-after checks for latency, memory, accessibility, and state preservation.
limitations: Provides guidance rather than a bundled profiler, executable scanner, or automated benchmark suite.
Needs project code, configuration, and relevant measurements to support project-specific conclusions.
TanStack-specific API work and React Three Fiber scenes require separate workflows.
Does not guarantee performance gains or make long JavaScript calculations asynchronous through React transitions.

use_cases.title: Review component correctness
use_cases.description: Check state ownership, component identity, effect cleanup, and loading behavior before merging component changes.

use_cases.title: Investigate slow interactions
use_cases.description: Interpret profiler and browser traces to select focused rendering, computation, or list optimizations.

use_cases.title: Assess React feature compatibility
use_cases.description: Review proposed React 19, compiler, and transition changes against installed versions and existing compatibility requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for state ownership, stable keys, and unnecessary effects. Explain each issue and suggest the smallest correction.

prompt_templates.title: Fix effect and loading behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this data-loading effect for races, cancellation, cleanup, and error handling. Preserve the existing data layer and recommend relevant tests.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a slow interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these React Profiler results and browser traces to diagnose slow input. Separate rendering from computation and layout, then propose a measured fix.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a version-sensitive optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this optimization against installed React, framework, and compiler configuration. Assess memoization, transitions, accessibility, and memory; define comparable before-and-after verification.

output_examples.input: Review a component that copies a prop-derived total into state through an effect.
output: The total duplicates information already available during render.
Calculate the total during render unless a separate user-editable value is required.
Verify that prop changes update the total without an additional synchronization effect.

output_examples.input: Typing remains slow after moving a large filtering calculation into a transition callback.
output: The transition callback runs immediately, so the filtering calculation still blocks input.
Keep controlled input updates urgent and evaluate a worker, chunked computation, or precomputation.
Compare the same interaction before and after, checking latency, pending feedback, and result correctness.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal to remove memoization after upgrading to React 19.
output: Installing React 19 does not configure React Compiler.
Confirm compiler setup and coverage before removing memoization.
Use comparable profiler measurements to determine whether the affected work still benefits from memoization.

best_practices: Inspect installed React, framework, data-layer, and compiler configuration before selecting APIs.
Base performance changes on representative measurements and compare the same interaction before and after.
Verify affected behavior, accessibility, loading states, and applicable lint, typecheck, build, and tests.
anti_patterns: Suppress effect dependency warnings instead of correcting unnecessary dependencies or synchronization.
Memoize every component or object without evidence that identity causes expensive downstream work.
Treat React transitions as a way to make a long synchronous calculation nonblocking.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does every component review require profiling?
faq.answer: No. Ordinary component edits use correctness guidance; slow interactions and proposed optimizations require relevant performance evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill require React 19?
faq.answer: No. It checks installed versions and preserves older compatibility requirements before recommending version-sensitive APIs.

faq.question: Does React 19 enable React Compiler automatically?
faq.answer: No. React Compiler is a separate build tool whose configuration and coverage must be verified.

faq.question: Can transitions prevent expensive filtering from blocking input?
faq.answer: Not by themselves. Transition callbacks run immediately; long calculations may need workers, chunking, or precomputation.

faq.question: Does this cover TanStack APIs or React Three Fiber scenes?
faq.answer: Those tasks use separate workflows. This skill focuses on React correctness, data-loading behavior, and rendering performance.
